title: DevX cadence & signal framework for SDKs, docs, and quickstarts curriculum
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: create a repeatable, measurable cadence and signal framework that drives adoption and retention for new SDKs, docs, and quickstarts. The output will be a modular curriculum (micro-lessons + code recipes + tracking plan) and a lightweight orchestration playbook teams can adopt when launching or iterating on SDKs or quickstarts.

Why now: onboarding velocity across SDKs and sample apps is inconsistent; we observe high initial traffic but low 7/14-day retention for several quickstarts. There is no shared signal definition for activation or an agreed cycle for curriculum updates. This increases time-to-first-success and causes engineers to miss opt-in product hooks.

Scope: design and pilot the cadence (monthly content sprints, weekly monitoring), define signal taxonomy (activation, first-success, retention, error signals), implement instrumentation for 3 pilot SDKs (JS, Python, Go), author 6 micro-lessons and 3 quickstart recipes, and ship a one-page orchestration playbook.

Out of scope: wholesale restructuring of core docs platform, major UI redesigns, or enterprise localization beyond English pilot.
acceptance_criteria: Signal spec documented and reviewed: definitions for 'first-success', '30-min activation', '7-day retention', and error-rate thresholds
Instrumentation events shipped for JS/Python/Go SDKs and visible in activation dashboard
Pilot curriculum: 6 micro-lessons and 3 quickstarts published with embedded code samples and tests
Orchestration playbook published in Confluence and validated by two engineering teams
Clear OKR mapping: +15% 7-day retention and +20% time-to-first-success reduction for pilot cohort
Post-pilot retro with lessons and roll-forward plan completed
milestones: 2025-12-20: instrumentation live in staging for pilots
2026-01-15: pilot retro and go/no-go for broader rollout
risks: Engineering bandwidth: competing infra priorities may delay event instrumentation
Metric noise: activation signals might be noisy without gating on sample app health
Adoption: partner teams may not follow the orchestration playbook exactly, reducing comparability
Localization: English-only pilot limits early global signals
